hypothesis: CIL's aggressive renewable energy targets (9.5 GW by FY 2029-30) face potential execution risks when comparing announced project pipeline status against current commissioning rates (e.g., only 200 MW commissioned of the 300 MW Khavda project as of July 2026).

research_questions.question: What is the granular commissioning status of the identified renewable portfolio projects?
missing: Updated schedule for Pugal, Jalaun, and BESS projects

research_questions.question: Does the capital expenditure (Capex) allocation align with the stated 9.5 GW target timeline?
metrics: Cumulative spend relative to project completion status (%)
missing: Breakdown of Capex by specific renewable project

evidence_ledger.excerpt_or_data_point: Company targets 9.5 GW renewable energy capacity by FY 2029-30. Includes specific projects: 875 MW Pugal Solar, 80 MW/320 MWh BESS Odisha, 600 MW Jalaun Solar, 300 MW Khavda (200 MW commissioned July 2026).
evidence_ledger.claim_supported: CIL renewable targets and specific project status
Progress status of 1.5 GW wind and 3 GW solar projects

checklist.step: Gather regulatory commissioning reports for CIL renewable assets
checklist.expected_evidence: Verification of 200 MW commissioning at Khavda and status of Pugal/Jalaun projects
cross_validation_sources: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) status updates
checklist.completion_criteria: Mapping of all identified projects to confirmed commissioned status

checklist.step: Analyze annual report Capex sections for renewable expenditure
checklist.expected_evidence: Annual spend data versus project delivery milestones
checklist.calculation: Spend per MW commissioned versus industry benchmarks
checklist.completion_criteria: Identification of any significant lag between capital deployment and asset commissioning

alternative_explanation: Project delays may result from sector-wide supply chain constraints, transmission grid connectivity bottlenecks, or land acquisition hurdles rather than specific company-level failure.
falsification_test: If commissioned capacity aligns with the projected 9.5 GW roadmap at reported interim milestones (as verified by third-party regulatory or industry trackers), the hypothesis of an execution gap is falsified.
